subject: Nimbus Dynamics: soft capacity hold and deploy readiness for POC (ND-7892)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus Dynamics - capacity gating for late-stage POC (soft hold request)

Team,

Quick context: Nimbus Dynamics (ND-7892) has turned on a late-stage POC ask — 8-week dedicated trial starting target week of 2026-10-03. They want a guaranteed dedicated pool for the POC to hit latency SLAs for their demo. Sales has negotiated primary terms but procurement needs confirmation we can place a soft hold on capacity until the contract is signed (target signature by 2026-09-29).

High-level ask:
- Can infra/ops confirm availability to hold 4 x A100-80GB (dedicated shard) in us-west-2 for window 2026-10-01 -> 2026-11-26 (8 weeks)?
- If a full hold is risky, what's the minimum committed reserve we can place (and latest cutoff for escalation)?
- Any conflicts with confirmed reserved pools in that window (EchoAI, OrionEdge)?

Constraints/notes:
- Deal_id: ND-7892; expected initial QPS pattern for POC: bursty inference with sustained tail latency < 150ms for 1k concurrent sessions.
- They require disabled autoscaler for the POC and a static shard to avoid noisy-neighbor variance.

Please reply with: availability window, recommended hold type (soft hold / provisional reserve / hard commit), and if needed an alternate plan (quantization or smaller instance suggestion) by EOD today so I can update the buyer (Linda) and include in the updated mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Dynamics - capacity gating for late-stage POC (soft hold request)

Monica —

We ran an inventory sweep and capacity simulation for us-west-2. Summary below:

- Raw availability: We can supply 4 x A100-80GB dedicated instances for the requested window starting 2026-10-01, but only as a provisional "soft hold" (no hard billing) until contract clears. Hard commit would require a one-month notice to reallocate existing reserved pools.
- Conflicts: EchoAI has a scheduled ramp beginning 2026-10-10 for a multi-week pilot; however, EchoAI's commit is for a different shard rack. If we place a soft hold now, we can guarantee the shard for ND-7892 through the POC period.
- Operational caveat: to reduce peak memory pressure we recommend enabling the 4-bit quantization profile for the POC model (reduces memory per head ~28%) — engineering has validated comparable accuracy for their LLM workload in staging. This gives us more flexibility if we need to shift capacity by 1 node.

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20260920.csv (includes per-rack free slot counts, current soft holds, and upcoming hard commits).

Recommendation: place a soft hold today and mark a hard-commit decision date at 2026-09-29 (aligned with their target signature). If procurement misses that date, we downgrade to preemptible backstop with 48h notice.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Compute Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Thanks Marcus — quick sizing validation from the SE side:

- Confirm 4 x A100-80GB is a conservative baseline given the requested latency profile, assuming the model is compiled with the suggested 4-bit quant profile.
- Network: plan for 8Gbps egress per node during peak demos; put a traffic-shaping rule for demo windows to avoid networking spikes affecting the shared infra.
- Autoscaler: agree on disabling autoscaler for the POC but we should enable a manual override for emergency 1-node scale (ops approval required).

Operational request: please open the internal capacity hold ticket (INFRA-4247) and set priority to P1-provisional. We need a hold marker that prevents reallocation and an explicit fallback that routes to preemptible nodes with a 48h warning.

I'll attach a short checklist for POC run-of-show and demo windows in the drive doc (link in Jira).

—Logan
